exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 Planning an Eco-holiday
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Rachel: Dad, for our holiday I'd love to do something that helps nature.
Dad: That sounds nice. What did you have in mind?
Rachel: There's an ecotourism trip where we can plant trees and count rhinos.
Dad: Plant trees? On a holiday? I just want to rest and read a book.
Rachel: But it also protects the animals, and we'd eat local food.
Dad: I can eat that kind of food at home, you know.
Rachel: Let's find a compromise, then. We could stay in one place near the reserve.
Dad: All right. You do the eco activities, and I'll relax and read.
Rachel: Perfect! And we could go on one walk through the jungle together.
Dad: Agreed. That way we both get the holiday we want.
exercises.translation_cn: Rachel 想过一个帮助自然的假期,参加能植树、数犀牛的生态旅游;爸爸只想休息看书;Rachel 说这还能保护动物、吃当地食物;两人各退一步:住在保护区附近,Rachel 做生态活动,爸爸放松看书,再一起穿过丛林散一次步。

questions.stem: What kind of holiday does Rachel want?
options: One on a busy city street.
One with no walking at all.

questions.stem: What does Dad want to do on holiday?
options: Plant as many trees as he can.

questions.stem: What do they decide to do about the food?
options: Eat the local food near the reserve.
Bring all their food from home.
Buy food only at the airport.

questions.stem: What is their compromise?
options: They will not go on holiday at all.
Rachel does the eco activities while Dad relaxes.
Dad will do every activity with Rachel.
Rachel will give up the eco activities.

questions.stem: What will they do together?
options: Go on one walk through the jungle.

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 The Sky Railway
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway is often called the Sky Railway.
Many experts once said that building it would be impossible.
It climbs to over five thousand metres above the sea.
Tanggula is the highest railway station anywhere on Earth.
Today the train races steadily across the high plateau.
exercises.translation_cn: 青藏铁路常被称为天路;许多专家曾说修建它是不可能的;它爬升到海拔五千多米;唐古拉是地球上最高的火车站;如今列车平稳地驶过高原。

questions.stem: What is the Qinghai-Tibet Railway often called?
What did many experts once say about it?
options: That building it would be impossible.
That it would be too short.

questions.stem: How high does the railway climb?
What is special about Tanggula?
options: It is the highest railway station on Earth.

questions.stem: How does the train move across the plateau today?
options: Very slowly and with great trouble.

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 An Interview for the Reef Job
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Manager: Welcome. So, why do you want to be the caretaker of the reef?
Lucy: I love the ocean, and I want to help protect such a special place.
Manager: The job lasts six months. Are you happy to live on a small island?
Lucy: Yes, completely. A place to stay is provided, isn't it?
Manager: It is, and your meals too. The salary is also negotiable.
Lucy: That's good to know. What would my main duties be?
Manager: Exploring the reef and telling the world about it through blogs and videos.
Lucy: I can do that. I've been writing a nature blog for two years.
Manager: Excellent. We give preference to people who can dive. Can you?
Lucy: Yes, I have a diving qualification, so I'm ready to start.
exercises.translation_cn: 经理面试 Lucy 申请珊瑚礁看护员;Lucy 说热爱海洋、想保护这个特别的地方;工作六个月、住在小岛,提供住处和三餐,薪水可协商;主要职责是探索珊瑚礁并通过博客视频对外宣传;Lucy 写自然博客已两年;公司优先考虑会潜水的人,Lucy 有潜水资格,随时可以开始。

questions.stem: Why does Lucy want the job?
options: She wants to help protect the reef.
She wants to leave the ocean behind.
She wants to build a hotel there.

questions.stem: What is provided for the caretaker?
options: A place to stay and meals.

questions.stem: What are the main duties of the job?
options: Exploring the reef and sharing it through blogs and videos.

questions.stem: What has Lucy been doing for two years?
Why is Lucy a strong candidate?
options: She has never seen the sea.

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 Saving the Antelopes
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The land near the railway is the home of the Tibetan antelope.
These animals travel a long way each year to give birth.
Builders left thirty-three passages under the line for them.
At first the shy animals were afraid to use the crossings.
Now they have been using the passages safely for years.
exercises.translation_cn: 铁路附近的土地是藏羚羊的家;这些动物每年长途迁徙去产仔;建设者在铁路下留了三十三条通道;起初害羞的动物不敢使用;如今它们已安全使用这些通道多年。

questions.stem: Whose home is the land near the railway?
Why do the antelopes travel a long way each year?
How many passages did the builders leave?
How did the animals feel about the crossings at first?
options: They were afraid to use them.

questions.stem: What has happened in recent years?
options: The antelopes have been using the passages safely.
The antelopes left the area forever.

exercises.title: U6 听力·对话 The White Beach Debate
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mr Lee: I really believe a new hotel at White Beach would be good for our city.
Maya: I understand, but I worry it might disturb the wildlife there.
Mr Lee: The fact is that a hotel would bring jobs and help the local economy.
Maya: Wouldn't you agree that the turtles laying eggs on the sand matter too?
Mr Lee: Of course they matter. I promise the design will be in harmony with nature.
Maya: More tourists also mean more cars and planes, and higher emissions.
Mr Lee: That's true. Let's find a compromise we can both accept.
Maya: As a compromise, we could build something smaller, away from the turtles' beach.
Mr Lee: I agree, but it must still attract enough visitors to be worthwhile.
Maya: Then let's protect the wildlife and welcome tourists at the same time.
exercises.translation_cn: 李先生认为在白沙滩建新酒店对城市有利;Maya 担心会扰乱野生动物;李先生说酒店能带来就业、促进经济;Maya 提醒在沙滩产卵的海龟也很重要;李先生承诺设计与自然和谐,但更多游客意味着更多车机和排放;两人寻求折中:把酒店建得更小、远离海龟海滩,同时既保护野生动物又欢迎游客。

questions.stem: What does Mr Lee want to build at White Beach?
What is Maya worried about?
options: That the hotel will be too cheap.
That the beach is too small.
That it might disturb the wildlife.

questions.stem: Which animals does Maya mention?
options: The turtles laying eggs on the sand.

questions.stem: Why does Maya say more tourists could be a problem?
options: They would be too noisy at night.
They would mean more cars, planes and emissions.

questions.stem: What compromise do they reach?
options: Build nothing and forbid all visitors.
Build something smaller, away from the turtles' beach.
Move the turtles to another country.

exercises.title: U6 听力·短文 Be a Responsible Traveller
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is some advice for anyone who loves to travel.
Try to be a responsible visitor wherever you go.
Leave each wild place just as beautiful as you found it.
Choose trips that help to conserve nature and support local people.
In this way, your holidays can protect the world instead of harming it.
exercises.translation_cn: 给所有热爱旅行的人一些建议:无论去哪里都做负责任的游客;让每一处荒野保持你见到时的美丽;选择有助于保护自然、支持当地人的旅行;这样,你的假期就能保护世界而非伤害它。

questions.stem: Who is this advice for?
What kind of visitor should you try to be?
How should you leave each wild place?
options: Just as beautiful as you found it.

questions.stem: What kind of trips should you choose?
options: Ones that use the most fuel.
Ones that help conserve nature and support local people.
Ones that cost the most money.

questions.stem: What can your holidays then do?
options: Protect the world instead of harming it.
